rationale: The workflow installs Elisp dependencies via Cask (`cask install`) in all three jobs (test-ubuntu matrix, test-macos, build-windows). This is a repeated dependency fetch that can be cached. Evidence from multiple experiments (P-LIT-GHA-CACHE) shows caching dependency downloads yields measurable savings (6-26% elapsed time reduction) across npm, pip, Go, and Gradle ecosystems. The pattern catalog confirms this optimization applies when 'repeated dependency fetching is measurable' and 'cache inputs include lockfile and environment' — here the Cask file serves as the lockfile and Emacs version/OS as environment. The change adds `actions/cache@v4` steps for the `.cask` directory (Ubuntu/macOS) and `~/.cask` (Windows) with keys incorporating runner OS, Emacs version, and hash of the Cask file. This preserves all build/test coverage and required checks while reducing redundant downloads.
